solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Journalist in hut putting out leader

indicators.note: putting out the leader means ejecting whatever stands at the front of the word

parts.note: a shack is a rough hut

explanation.surface: A reporter holed up in a hut, turning out its chief.
explanation.walkthrough: SHACK loses its first letter to leave HACK.
explanation.definitionFit: Hack is an informal, often slighting, word for a newspaper writer.

clue.text: Brother entertained by the divine George is a flowery type

indicators.note: to be entertained by a host is to be taken in by them, so one word sits inside another

parts.note: George Herbert, the seventeenth-century poet and clergyman
short form of brother

explanation.surface: A monk is put up by a clergyman named George, who happens to be rather florid.
explanation.walkthrough: George Herbert was an English priest and devotional poet, hence 'divine'; the brother splits his surname after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Herb Robert is a wild geranium with small pink flowers, so it is a flowering plant.

clue.text: Encrypted hoax written by newspaperman?

parts.note: cod as a verb means to hoax or kid someone
ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: A spoof message put together by a journalist, apparently in cipher.
explanation.definitionFit: Something coded has been put into a cipher, the same as encrypted.

clue.text: Famous actress, girl reportedly in special garment?

definitions.note: a tailor-made is a made-to-measure suit; the question mark flags the noun use

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so the words are judged by their sound rather than their spelling

parts.note: Elizabeth Taylor, the film star
maid is an old word for a girl

explanation.surface: A film star and a young woman in some distinctive outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: A tailor-made garment is cut specially for one wearer, so it is a bespoke piece of clothing.

clue.text: A river with bats and sick old animal

parts.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for river
bats is slang for crazy
sick means unwell
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A riverbank scene with bats and an ailing elderly creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bats' looks like more animals but means crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: The armadillo is an armoured mammal of the Americas, a straightforward example of an animal.

clue.text: Joins a course for outdoor sporting types

definitions.meaning: first meaning: connects, as a verb

definitions.text: a course for outdoor sporting types
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a seaside golf course

explanation.surface: Someone signing up for a class aimed at outdoorsy athletes.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb for connecting things and also the name of a coastal golf course.

clue.text: Support this writer has to be rebellious?

parts.note: a rest is a support, as for a cue or an arm
the setter saying 'I have', contracted to I've

explanation.surface: A writer asking for backing in order to make trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This writer' is the setter, so 'this writer has' is I'VE.
explanation.definitionFit: Restive means restless and resisting control, close to unruly; the question mark admits the stretch.

clue.text: Mistakenly alter a top building for self-catering guests

indicators.note: something done mistakenly comes out wrong, so the letters end up in a different order

parts.note: the letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A builder botches a conversion of the top floor of a guest house.
explanation.definitionFit: An aparthotel offers serviced flats with kitchens, so guests cater for themselves in a hotel-style block.

clue.text: Regular time to relax from the day job?

definitions.text: time to relax from the day job?
definitions.meaning: second meaning: an old poetic word for ...

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is archaic, which the question mark acknowledges.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means level or steady, and in old poetry it is a short form of evening, when work is done.

clue.text: Slithery thing left a mark climbing tree

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing means the letters run upward, read bottom to top

parts.note: an eel is a slippery fish
L is the abbreviation for left
taken as written
M for the German mark

explanation.surface: A snake leaves a trail as it goes up a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: A mallee is an Australian scrubby eucalyptus.
explanation.definitionFit: Mallee names several low, many-stemmed eucalyptus species of Australia, so it is a kind of tree.

clue.text: Wines served with fruit mainly and fish

indicators.note: mainly means most of the word but not all, so its final letter drops away

parts.note: reds are red wines
an almond is a fruit (a nut)

explanation.surface: A menu pairing wines with a fruit course and a fish course.
explanation.definitionFit: Red salmon, or sockeye, is a Pacific salmon species, so it is a kind of fish.

clue.text: A lot row, ending in lake

parts.note: a spat is a petty quarrel

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its final letter, so only that letter is kept

parts.note: the last letter of lake

explanation.surface: Plenty of rowing, finishing up in a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' suggests oars and the lake, but it is a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A spate is a sudden flood or large number of things, so it means a great many.

clue.text: Debauched king was first to embrace tot

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in one's arms, so one word wraps around another

parts.note: R for rex, Latin king
to have led is to have been in front
to tot up is to add

explanation.surface: A dissolute monarch who got in first to hug a small child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tot' looks like a small child but is the verb meaning to sum up.
explanation.definitionFit: Raddled describes a face worn and ravaged by dissipation, so it fits a debauched look.

clue.text: English in Tonbridge? Only some wanted Eastern religion!

indicators.note: wanting only some of the letters means just a part of the run of words is taken

parts.note: letters running across the words

explanation.surface: In a Kentish town, only a few people want an Asian faith.
explanation.walkthrough: Tonbridge is a town in Kent, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Shinto is the native religion of Japan, so it is a faith from the East.

clue.text: Dogs you upset beginning to howl in land by manor?

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so these letters go within the next word

parts.note: the land around a big house

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, so just that letter is taken

parts.note: first letter of howl

indicators.note: in a down entry, upset means turned over, so the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: old form of you

explanation.surface: Dogs around a country house, upset by someone and starting to howl.
explanation.walkthrough: The archaic form of 'you' is the one wanted here; the land by a manor house is the estate around it, which takes in the other letters after its second.
explanation.definitionFit: Greyhounds are a slender breed of racing dog, so they are an example of dogs.

clue.text: What locations just outside Midland city do for sheep

parts.note: places just outside a city border it
Leicester is a city in the English Midlands

explanation.surface: A question about what the outskirts of a Midlands city do for sheep farming.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads cryptically as 'what places on the edge of Leicester do': they border Leicester.
explanation.definitionFit: The Border Leicester is a long-wool British breed, so it names a type of sheep.

clue.text: Lived it up — sore and tired, needing a change?

indicators.note: something needing a change must be altered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of sore and tired, with and as a joining word

explanation.surface: After a big night, someone is aching and exhausted and wants a change.
explanation.definitionFit: To roister is to revel noisily, so roistered means partied hard.

clue.text: Haughty claim of fairy to dismiss mostly

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a fairy saying 'I'm peri'; a peri is a fairy of Persian legend
to oust is to remove or throw out

explanation.surface: A proud sprite insists on being sent away, more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fairy' tempts toward IMP, but the claim is I'M PERI.
explanation.definitionFit: Imperious means domineering and arrogant, much the same as haughty.

clue.text: Report of cricket's unfortunate downfall?

parts.note: surface reading: news of the collapse of a cricket side
setter's reading: a fall of rain on the field, causing the match to halt

explanation.walkthrough: 'Downfall' is literal: precipitation falling down halts the cricket, and the scoreboard announcement reports it.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the standard notice when bad weather suspends a cricket match.

clue.text: Street traveller, no dawdler?

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street
a rider travels on horseback or by bike

explanation.surface: A pedestrian in the road who doesn't hang about.
explanation.definitionFit: A strider walks with long, purposeful steps, the opposite of someone lingering.

clue.text: Show contempt for Greek island parties?

parts.note: to dis is to disrespect
Cos, or Kos, is in the Dodecanese

explanation.surface: Sneering at the party scene on a Greek holiday isle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For' here simply joins the two halves.
explanation.definitionFit: Discos are dance parties with recorded music, so the word stands for parties.

clue.text: One watching Casualty in US chasing celebrity

indicators.note: to chase is to follow behind, so this piece comes after the other

parts.note: a star is a famous person
the American emergency room, the British casualty department

explanation.surface: A viewer of a hospital drama pursuing a famous actor.
explanation.walkthrough: Casualty is both a UK hospital department and a TV drama; in America the department is the ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A starer is someone who gazes fixedly, so a person watching.

clue.text: Drive back from dance, parking inside

indicators.note: inside means placed within, so one letter sits in the middle of a word

parts.note: a reel is a lively Scottish dance
P is the sign for parking

explanation.surface: Driving home from a dance and parking indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: To repel an attack is to repulse it, forcing the attackers back.

clue.text: Dish of duck gentleman sent back with dry egg

indicators.note: sent back means returned the way it came, so the word is read right to left

parts.note: sir is a form of address for a gentleman
a duck is a zero score in cricket
TT, teetotal, means not drinking
an egg is round like an O

explanation.surface: A restaurant scene: a gentleman returns a duck dish along with an overcooked egg.
explanation.walkthrough: SIR reversed gives RIS, which leads the answer. Duck is zero in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Risotto is an Italian rice dish, so it is a dish of food.

clue.text: A huge fellow with no name turned up in forest

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means flipped to read bottom to top
having no name means the abbreviation for name is taken out

parts.note: taken as written
a giant is an enormous man

explanation.surface: A nameless giant shows up in the woods.
explanation.walkthrough: GIANT loses N (name) to give GIAT; with A in front that is AGIAT, reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: The taiga is the vast coniferous forest belt of northern Russia and Canada.

clue.text: Future source of beef, possibly a bit of shank?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the back of the lower leg

explanation.walkthrough: Shank is the leg below the knee, of which the fleshy back part is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names young cattle, which may grow into beef, and the muscular rear of the lower leg.

clue.text: Engineers coming in to help broadcast

indicators.note: coming in means entering, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: aid means help
the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: Technicians arriving to assist with a transmission.
explanation.definitionFit: A programme that has been aired has been transmitted on radio or TV.

clue.text: Voting for what's proposed brings advancement

parts.note: pro means in favour of
a motion is a proposal put to a meeting

explanation.surface: Backing a proposal gets you ahead at work.
explanation.definitionFit: Promotion is advancement in rank or position, a synonym.

clue.text: Supporter of union supplied with rota, saving time

parts.note: fed means provided with food or goods
an era is a period of time
a rota is a list of duties

explanation.surface: A union backer handed a duty roster that saves them time.
explanation.walkthrough: The blogger reads 'saving' as containing, but the time simply sits in front of the rota; take it as loose positioning.
explanation.definitionFit: A federalist advocates a federation, a union of states under a central government.

clue.text: Insect we hear in the country

indicators.note: we hear means as spoken, so the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: a louse is a small parasitic insect

explanation.surface: A bug that we're told lives out in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: Laos is often said like louse.
explanation.definitionFit: Laos is a landlocked nation of Southeast Asia, so it names a country.
